newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP ON TUESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted slightly firmer on Tuesday and dealers attributed this to reduced liquidity in the system.
"There were no maturities yesterday and the market looks squarish. There isn't much trade going on at the moment," commented one.
The dealers added however that the tightness in the market would only be short-lived since sizeable volumes of maturities were expected on Thursday and Friday.

They maintained that an ongoing strike by civil servants demanding salary increments from the government had not yet influenced market activity but added that financial losses incurred through the action might have a long-term effect.
Meanwhile on Tuesday, discount houses were buying treasury bills from the central Reserve Bank at 22.66 percent and selling them on the open market at 22.60 percent, up from 22.50.

NCD bills redeemable within 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought firmer at 23.85 from 23.65 percent and sold at 23.50 percent from 23.25 percent while bankers acceptances edged up to 23.25 and 23 percent from 23.15 and 22.85 percent.
Call money fluctuated between 22.5 and 22.75 percent after peaking at 22.5 percent on Monday. -- Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9.
